symptoms: Third or fourth leaf from top yellows and withers; split cane reveals internal tissue reddened with characteristic white transverse bands perpendicular to stalk; alcoholic odor.
management: Consult local agricultural university / KVK package of practices for registered treatment.
prevention: Practice crop rotation, field hygiene, and use certified seeds.

symptoms: Characteristic visual lesions, discoloration or foliar distress associated with Bacterial Blight.
management: Isolate affected foliage, apply approved bio-fungicide or targeted treatment.
prevention: Implement crop rotation, avoid water stagnation, and sanitize farm implements regularly.

management: Install pheromone traps and apply bio-control agents.

correction: Foliar spray of Ferrous Sulphate (FeSO4) @ 10g/L + Citric Acid @ 1g/L (to prevent oxidation) or Fe-EDTA @ 1.5g/L twice at 10-day intervals.

healthy_signs: Robust, thick cane stalks or deep-lobed green leaves with vigorous growth
Strong internodes free from boreholes or internal red rot
Clean foliar canopy with active photosynthesis
Sturdy root anchoring with no basal wilt
management: Uproot and burn severely wilted or red-rot infected canes/plants immediately
Drench border rows with biocontrol formulations to create protective barrier zones
Follow integrated pest management (IPM) guidelines strictly
prevention: Select healthy setts/seeds from certified nurseries or disease-free mother plants
Adopt drip irrigation to avoid excess soil moisture around root crowns
Practice deep summer ploughing to expose soil-borne resting spores and pupae
Rotate with green manure crops such as sunnhemp or daincha
